difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the boundary identity for the tree polynomial Q, printed as Lemma 4.1 in the published version (source0.tex lines 2059--2062; the environment is unlabelled in the source), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 2064--2090. The paper declares eighteen theorem-like environments (source0.tex lines 11--32) and uses no theorem environment anywhere: its numbered results are propositions, lemmas, definitions, examples, one corollary, one conjecture and one List. Of the four propositions, Proposition 3.1 (an extension of a quasigroup by an affine quasigroup is a quasigroup, lines 598--600) is proved by checking one typical case and declaring the rest similar, Proposition 3.4 (label Second, lines 678--682) is proved by a sixteen-line substitution that reads the second boundary map off the homomorphism condition, and Propositions 4.3 and 4.4 carry eight-line and three-line proofs. The strongest complete author proof in the paper is therefore the twenty-seven-line proof of the unlabelled Lemma 4.1 counted here, and the environment in which that result is printed is a lemma. The proof is complete given the retained context: it expands (d_2 o Q)(T) over the internal vertices of the rooted binary tree from Q(T)=sum h_v(t,s)g(v) and d_2(x,y)=tx+sy-xy; it exhibits the two local cancellations (the blue term t^{i(v)+1}s^{j(v)} gbar(v_L) of d_2(g(v)) against the blue term -t^{i(v)+1}s^{j(v)} gbar(v_L) of d_2(g(v_L)), and the red term t^{i(v)}s^{j(v)+1} gbar(v_R) against the final term of d_2(g(v_R))); it records that a child which is a leaf leaves a non-cancelling term t^{i(v_L)}s^{j(v_L)} gbar(v_L), which is exactly the leaf sum of the statement; and it observes that the only surviving internal term is the root term -gbar(r). Supplying the definition of an affine quasigroup, the affine identities of Lemma 3.2, the definition of equivalent extensions together with d_2(x,y)=tx+sy-xy, and the paper's own definitions of Q, g and gbar, the argument still has to be carried out: it is a telescoping cancellation over an arbitrary rooted binary tree in which the surviving terms must be identified by hand from the t,s-weights i(v) and j(v). The result is not decoration: Corollary 4.2 is deduced from it two lines later and it is the identity that makes d_2 o d_3 = 0, and hence the BMq chain complex, exist. No qualifying examination poses it, which places it in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.
